quotes.text: when a shore has proven it hoards. Then a smaller cast is a teacher, not a punishment.
Return half and a thread more.
In the sixth season of the Mist-River
I read the tapestry each weaver leaves behind.
The mist deceives the eye before the heart does.
Do you not fear that one day the far shore will keep it all?
Why not keep more? The stranger cannot see you.
Return more than half.
They were wronged, yet they answered the next caster with open hands.
What if they hold back from you now?

note: Weaver Suna and daughter at Mist-River; law restated each season; smaller cast only to proven hoarders as teacher; son's 'send nothing' rejected.

quotes.text: Only a heart that withheld again and again did they answer with caution.
Return more than half. Doubt the wind before the hand.
In the fifth season of the Well of Three Waters
Let the record speak.
Judge the season, not the gust.
Why give beyond the even line?
then added a little more to Doran's side
What if the Wind of Murmurs thins what comes back?

note: Well of Three Waters, notches on the rim; turn only from those who keep taking; grandson's 'return less' rejected; mend without keeping count.

quotes.text: A drawer who punishes every thin bucket turns the mist into a quarrel.
Return a trickle and pocket the rest. No one will see through this mist.
Meet proven hands with full baskets. Return half and more.
I do not remember faces, for the Wind shuffles them. I remember deeds.
Perhaps the mist swallowed a handful on the way down.
No one will see through this mist.
Why lower everything again? Luck may not hold twice.
Give fully, return half and more
This one was repaid thinly and kept giving anyway.
What if the stranger hoards?

note: Sanu at the tripling well; nephew and a scoffing traveler urge thin returns, rejected; carved stones record deeds; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: Answer crooked hands fairly but never with nothing.
Return half and a little more. Mend what the wind frays.
On the sixth dawn of the silver-loom age
Across the loom waited a weaver whose record the hills knew well.
Assume the wind, not the heart.
Is there ever a caster whose bundle you would answer thinly?
Return half and a little more.
If the hills showed a weaver who always kept most of their threads, I would return only a fair share of what truly came.

note: Aro's silver loom, Kesh and sister; siblings' thin-return advice rejected; R10 states fair share but never nothing to hoarders.

quotes.text: Pour small but never nothing to crooked ones.
Read before you pour. Pour fully to straight hands.
In the seventh season, Asha stood on the eastern end
The marks are carved by deeds
One short basket is the fog. Many short baskets would be the heart.
Is there ever a shore where you would pour less?
Why not keep more? He will never know your face.
She sent back half and a little more, because Asha had risked everything and should not be poorer for it.
If Mirren sent more than I saw, my return still lifts her above her five.

note: Asha reads tally-sticks on the willow; cousin's doubts answered; small but never nothing to hoarders, door stays open.

quotes.text: Withhold only from those who always take.
Cast fully to faithful hands. Return half and a little more.
In the sixth season, the weavers of Tavi began tying knots
Your knots walk ahead of you, into every dawn.
The mist lies, not our neighbors. Judge by many seasons, not one fog.
Why do we tie knots at all, if the Wind pairs us with strangers?
sent the larger half back across the loom
"You trusted first," he said.
Do not punish a stranger for another's greed.
But what if one day the frame shows grasping hands?

note: Tavi's loom, knots on the frame; withhold only from those who always take; mend threads others broke.

quotes.text: To hands that grasp, I would give less and watch what they learn.
give fully, return half and a little more, forgive the mist, and mend the losses you cannot see.
On the sixth night, the potter Dray stood below the crossroads
No one could see faces through the mist, but everyone could see hands.
One flicker is weather, not betrayal.
You could keep it all. No one would see through this fog.
You have given fully before. Will you always?
When much is given, return more than half.
What if tonight is the night they turn?

note: Lantern of Kindling, glowing palms record deeds; mother's 'pour nothing' rejected; give less to grasping hands only stated R9.

quotes.text: Turn cautious only toward hands that stay empty, season after season.
Some spirits grew bitter, cried betrayal, and poured nothing ever after.
Return half and more when you stand below.
In the seventh season, the Wind paired Oru with a familiar shimmer.
The water remembers deeds, not promises,
Read their deeds, not their luck.
That thinness was done *to* them, not *by* them,
But how can I trust a partner I cannot see?
Return more than was given, so the giver never regrets the pouring.
Then give first. The one upstream holds the power to begin.

note: Tripling River spirits merge with Mist-River and Well myths; shimmer records deeds; turn cautious only toward persistently empty hands.

phrase: be the same weaver/keeper on both shores (return half and a little more)
note: Also cross-agent world-sharing: Well of Three Waters (A2,A3,A7,A8), Mist-River/Suna/Tirra (A1,A8); 'forgive the fog' refrain in all.
